newsitem.title: USA: Epitope says unit to recall strawberries.
newsitem.headline: Epitope says unit to recall strawberries.

text.p: Epitope Inc said its Andrew and Williamson Sales Co unit began a voluntary recall of frozen, sliced strawberries shipped to distributors for institutional use in six states because they were associated with an occurence of Hepatitis A in some Michigan schools.

The unit would recall 13 lots of strawberries, the company said. The lots subject to the recall were shipped early in December 1996, shortly before Epitope acquired Andrew and Williamson, it said. The berries were grown in Mexico and processed in San Diego, Epitope said.

"The health and well-being of the public is A&W's foremost concern," Epitope chief executive Adolph Ferro said. "While it is not certain that the lots being recalled are contaminated, we want to eliminate all possible risk to consumers."
He said the customers had been notified and the company was cooperating with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
